the ultra scale‐down method can be applied to predict clarification of cell broths by continuous centrifugation, and flocculated cell broths are more easily clarified than homogenized cell broths.

the ultra scale‐down characterization of harvested E. coli cell broths is a valuable approach to understanding the impact of conditioning methods for harvested cell broths on the clarification by continuous centrifugation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and processing of E. coli cell lysate and the recovery of the expressed recombinant protein.
the development and application of ultra scale-down techniques to the characterisation of bioprocesses.
the processing of cell broths from recombinant E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of flocculation as a pre‐treatment method for cell harvest broths containing a product that has been released into solution can lead to a significant improvement in the performance of the subsequent clarification step using continuous flow centrifugers.
the use of flocculation as a pre-treatment for harvested cell broths is an attractive proposition.
the use of flocculation to pre‐treat the harvested cell broth has been demonstrated to be a potentially effective method to aid clarification of the material using centrifugation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ultra scale-down centrifuge can be used to assess the impact of different cell disruption methods for the recovery of proteins from E. coli cell lysate.
the ultra scale‐down approach is a valuable method to assess the impact of different pre‐treatment methods for the recovery of proteins from E. coli cell lysates.
ultra scale-down centrifugation is a useful tool for the characterization of cell broths.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clarification performance of continuous flow centrifuging can be predicted from the particle size distribution of the harvested broth, the viscosity, and solids fraction.
the clarification of cell broths can be improved by the use of pre‐treatment methods.
flocculation can be an effective method for pre-treatment of harvested cell broths prior to clarification.
